questions.stem: A team needs to ingest Salesforce objects into Unity Catalog tables and wants the most automation, with no code to maintain. Which approach does Databricks recommend starting with?

options.text: An Auto Loader stream reading CSV exports from cloud storage
A notebook calling the Salesforce REST API on a schedule
A Lakeflow Connect managed connector for Salesforce
COPY INTO from a nightly export

questions.explanation: Databricks recommends starting with the most managed layer; Lakeflow Connect's SaaS connectors ingest from applications including Salesforce, and managed connectors produce ingestion pipelines governed by Unity Catalog.

questions.stem: JSON files land in cloud object storage throughout the day, up to millions of files per hour, and must be processed once each as they arrive. Which method fits?

options.text: Auto Loader (the cloudFiles source)
A manual file upload in the workspace UI
A managed database connector using change data capture
A one-off CREATE TABLE AS SELECT each hour over the whole folder

questions.explanation: Auto Loader provides a Structured Streaming source called cloudFiles that processes new files as they arrive, scales to millions of files per hour, and processes data exactly once.

questions.stem: A source system is a SQL Server database, and the team wants ongoing incremental ingestion of changes into governed tables. Which choice fits best?

options.text: Auto Loader pointed at the database's data files
A file connector for SharePoint
A REST client in a notebook that reads the whole table each run
A Lakeflow Connect database connector, which ingests using change data capture

questions.explanation: Lakeflow Connect database connectors ingest data from relational databases including MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server using change data capture.

questions.stem: A SQL-only team wants scalable incremental ingestion from cloud object storage. Which does Databricks recommend over COPY INTO?

options.text: INSERT OVERWRITE from a view
CREATE STREAMING TABLE
A scheduled CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT
CONVERT TO DELTA

questions.explanation: SQL examples for incremental ingestion from cloud object storage use CREATE STREAMING TABLE syntax, which Databricks names the recommended alternative to COPY INTO.

questions.stem: No managed connector exists for a team's source system. What does Databricks suggest?

options.text: Wait for a managed connector, because other methods aren't governed by Unity Catalog
Copy the data by hand into a workspace file
Drop down to the next layer, such as SQL and Spark APIs, which trade some automation for broader source support
Use a Lakeflow Connect file connector for any source

questions.explanation: Start with the most managed layer; if it doesn't satisfy your requirements, for example if it doesn't support your source, drop down to the next layer. SQL and Spark APIs trade some automation for broader source support and customization.

questions.stem: An Auto Loader stream lists a very large input folder on every run, and the team wants to cut those listing costs. What does Databricks recommend for most workloads?

options.text: File notification mode using file events
Directory listing mode with a shorter trigger interval
Reading the folder with spark.read in a batch job
Turning off schema inference

questions.explanation: By default Auto Loader uses directory listing mode, but Databricks recommends file notification mode using file events for most workloads; it can reduce cloud costs by avoiding directory listing altogether.
